Cultural food story
Black-eyed peas (cowpeas) traveled the Atlantic with enslaved West Africans and became a cornerstone of Gullah Geechee and Southern foodways — eaten for luck and resilience.
Open in Food Roots Atlas →
Whole-food advantage
Because this is whole food — not isolated powder — the fiber and fat blunt your blood-sugar spike. Eating the greens and peas before the rice can lower the post-meal glucose response by roughly 29–37%.
AI confidence & assumptions
Overall confidence Medium. Assumed 1 tbsp red palm oil and home portions. Photo-based estimates are not laboratory measurements.

Training as ritual
Lifting doesn't have to be a mirror sport. Open with breath, name what the session is for, move with rhythm, close with stillness — the same sets become practice instead of punishment.
Farm-Fitness Library
Push & Carry
Real farm actions, trained with intention. Progress by adding distance or load — not by grinding yourself down.
350–700
cal / hr farm work
420
farmer's walk cal/hr
6.0
MET · vigorous
The rotational core of farm work
Real labor is rotation: hoeing, scything, tossing compost, twisting under load. Train it deliberately — chops, rotational throws and anti-rotation holds — so the spine turns through the hips instead of the low back. Two sets each, slow and controlled, before the carries.
Breathing
Exhale on the lift; brace without breath-holding. Stop if you feel dizzy — noted for your profile.
Move · elder strength
Reclaiming power at every age
Muscle isn't vanity here — it's independence, balance and the strength to serve the village.
After 30 we lose 3–8% of muscle per decade, faster after 60. Resistance training is the only proven way to halt and reverse it.
{{ elderSessionLine }}

Minimum effective dose

VariableMinimumOptimal
{{ d.v }}{{ d.min }}{{ d.opt }}
Plant protein for muscle preservation
Elders need more, not less: 1.2–1.5 g/kg daily to overcome anabolic resistance — about 25–35g per meal, with 2.5–2.8g leucine to trigger repair. Lentils, hemp, tempeh-free options and evening protein all count.
{{ elderProteinLine }}

Strength for daily life

{{ m.move }}
→ {{ m.adl }}
Farm work counts: digging, water-carries and compost-turning are resistance training when structured with rest and progressive load.
Balance is the fall-prevention drill
Two sessions a week of single-leg stands, heel-to-toe walking and slow sit-to-stands cut fall risk more than strength work alone. Hold a counter, count to twenty, breathe out on the effort — and never train balance alone if you feel unsteady.
Well established Source: Elder Plant-Based Fitness →
Move · land-based traditions
Ancestral movement & dance
Strength, power and endurance are ancestral — encoded in dance and ritual long before the barbell. Fitness as remembrance, not punishment.
Warrior lineages drawn on
Zulu Maasai Dahomey Capoeira Taíno Garifuna
Train to the drum
Moving to rhythm isn't just culture — syncing effort to a beat (BPM) improves endurance, with athletes sustaining work about two minutes longer. Set the tempo to the work: slow drum for strength, faster for conditioning.

How to know it worked
You should finish looser than you started and no sorer tomorrow. Sharp pain, tingling or a joint that clicks painfully means back off that hold — range is earned slowly and never forced.
Move · chair-supported
Seated & adaptive
A full circuit that never asks you onto the floor. For flare-up days, recovery weeks, chair users, and anyone training beside an elder.
This is not the easy version. Seated work builds real strength when you slow the tempo and hold the last inch — the chair removes balance risk, not effort.

Two rounds, then stop
Run the six in order, rest two minutes, run them once more. If a chair with arms is what you have, use them — pushing through the arms is a legitimate progression, not cheating.

Where are you right now?
Safety gate

Your care team leads here

Before we adapt any plan, confirm you've discussed exercise and nutrition with your provider.

Stop & seek care if you notice
Vaginal bleeding · fluid leaking · regular painful contractions · chest pain or breathlessness · dizziness or fainting · calf pain or swelling · reduced fetal movement.
What we adapt

Gentle, clinician-approved shifts

Movement
Keep strength you already have; skip new maxes. Avoid long flat-on-back work later in pregnancy, no breath-holding (brace on the exhale), and add pelvic-floor awareness to every set.
Nourishment
Extra iron, folate and B12; steady protein across the day; plenty of water. Your plates lead with cowpeas, callaloo, moringa and fortified plant milk — labeled clearly, no herbs contraindicated in pregnancy.
Pelvic floor & breath
Daily connection breathing over max effort. A pelvic-floor therapist referral is offered rather than assumed — the app never prescribes.
Postpartum rebuilding

Return, don't rush

1
Wait for your provider's clearance (often ~6 weeks, longer after a C-section).
2
Rebuild the core and pelvic floor first; watch for diastasis (doming) before loading.
3
Fuel recovery and, if nursing, extra calories, fluids, iron and B12. Rest is training.
Your Growth Journal will celebrate function — "carried the baby up the stairs pain-free" — never a rush back to an old body.

Butter-Bean, Collard & Sorghum Bowl

⏱ 30 min· 4 servings· low glycemic load
How your blood sugar responds
— This meal (steady)-- Refined carbs (spike)
17g

31g

Why it stays steady
›Intact sorghum + bean fiber slows glucose release — no refined flour.
›Eat greens & beans first, grain last — food order can cut the post-meal spike ~29–37%.
›Magnesium, chromium & potassium support insulin sensitivity.

Ingredients

1 cup sorghum · 1½ cups butter beans · 3 cups collards · 1 onion · 2 tomatoes · 1 tbsp olive oil · garlic, ginger, cumin · squeeze of lime
Swaps: sorghum → fonio or barley · butter beans → black-eyed peas · add avocado for extra healthy fat.
Managing diabetes?
Whole-food eating can meaningfully improve glycemic control, but if you take insulin or glucose-lowering medication, changes can affect your dose. Coordinate with your clinician — the Council supports, it doesn't prescribe or adjust medication.
Emerging evidence Source: Plant-Based Strategies for T2 Diabetes →

Mushroom Mastery
Food and medicine in one body — meaty textures for the plate, studied compounds for recovery.
The sunlight trick
Set any mushroom gills-up in midday sun for 30–60 minutes. It makes vitamin D the way your skin does — and keeps it through cooking.
{{ m.name }}
{{ m.ev }}
{{ m.role }}
{{ m.use }}
Grow your own
Oyster mushrooms fruit on used coffee grounds or straw in a bucket — harvest in 2–3 weeks, indoors, year-round. The cheapest protein you'll ever grow.
Wild mushrooms are different
Never eat a foraged mushroom without expert, in-person identification — lookalikes can be deadly. Buy cultivated, or walk with a trained guide.

Journey · private
Sexual Vitality & Hormones
Desire is a vital sign — built from minerals, sleep, circulation and safety. Sacred in many of our traditions, never shameful here.
Private by default
Excluded from exports. The Council only considers this area if you allow it.
The energy circuit
•Heavy hip and leg work — carries, hinges, farm labor — is the strongest natural hormonal signal you can send
•Sex hormones are made while you sleep — under 7 hours quietly drains them
•Chronic stress steals the raw material for desire — calm is not a luxury, it's hormonal maintenance
Foods our traditions reach for
{{ v.name }}
{{ v.ev }}
{{ v.why }}
Practices, not performances
•Pelvic-floor and deep-core strength — bridges, breath-led bracing — supports function at every age
•A long-exhale breath together downshifts both nervous systems before intimacy
•Consent and honest words are the foundation — energy flows where safety lives
Your body, your framing
Hormonal guidance here separates physiology from identity — cycle-aware or not, gender-affirming always, and shaped only by what you choose to share.
Strength and desire share a bloodstream
Heavy compound lifts, sprint work and sleep move testosterone and circulation more than any powder does. Beets and citrus for nitric oxide, pumpkin seeds for zinc, and enough carbohydrate to train hard — under-eating flattens desire faster than anything else.
When to see a clinician
Persistent low desire, erectile changes, painful sex or cycle shifts deserve real care — they can signal iron, thyroid, B12 or cardiovascular issues. This screen supports; it never diagnoses.
Traditional use Source: Sexual Vitality & Strength →
Nourish · the village table
Kids & Family Nutrition
Growing bodies, elder bones and training adults — one pot, portioned differently. Food as culture and celebration, never restriction.
{{ selFamily.name }}'s plate priorities
•{{ p.t }}
One pot, three plates
Cook one base — bean stew, grain, greens. Then portion: the child's plate gets extra coconut and avocado for energy density, the training adult gets a second scoop of beans, the elder gets greens chopped fine and the biggest protein anchor.
Kid-approved smoothies
{{ kidFlagLine }}
{{ k.name }}
{{ k.p }} · {{ k.kcal }} kcal
{{ k.base }}
{{ k.flagLabel }}
Non-negotiables for growing bodies
•B12 daily — fortified milks or drops; no plant food covers it reliably
•Vitamin D through the dark months, dosed by age
•Iron needs jump in growth spurts and teen cycles — beans + vitamin C every day
Raise growers, not dieters
No calorie talk at the table. Kids learn food as strength and story — give them their own microgreen tray to water, a market job on Saturdays, a wooden spoon in the pot.
Smoothies that actually build
Blend for density, not volume: a nut or seed butter for calories, a fortified milk for B12 and calcium, frozen mango or banana for sweetness, and a handful of pea or melon microgreens they helped grow. Serve in a real glass — it reads as a treat, not a supplement.
Grow with a pediatrician
A plant-based childhood thrives with growth tracked by a pediatric clinician and supplements dosed by age — this screen plans meals, it never replaces that care.
Emerging evidence Source: Vegan Smoothies for Growing Children →

Foodways Codex
Ten regional volumes in three families of exchange. Each separates what was always plant-based from what has been adapted — and names the evidence carrying the claim.

dish classifications
How every dish is labelled
Traditionally vegan Traditionally plant-forward Adaptation Diasporic reconstruction Diasporic innovation Contemporary innovation
A dish that was always plant-based is never called “veganised.” A dish that was not is never rewritten to look like it was.
{{ fam.t }}
{{ fam.n }}
{{ fam.s }}
These volumes synthesise published culinary history, archaeobotany, nutrition science and community documentation — they are not fieldwork we conducted. Where sources disagree, the Codex shows the disagreement instead of picking a winner.
See the source library →
Companion to the Foodways Codex

Pantry Codex

The Foodways Codex asks what a dish always was. The Pantry Codex asks the same of the ingredient — where it was domesticated, who was paid for it, and which claims on the label the evidence actually carries.
{{ pantryVolTotal }}
pantry volumes
{{ pantryEntryTotal }}
graded entries
6
classification axes
How an entry is built
One canonical scientific name, community names at equal prominence
Every ingredient is classified on six axes at once — scientific, cultural, agricultural, nutritional, chemical and commercial. Fonio is findi, fundi, acha and “hungry rice” across different Sahelian language communities, all mapping to one key. Callaloo means amaranth in Jamaica and taro leaves in Trinidad; okra is at least two species, Abelmoschus esculentus and the West African allotetraploid A. caillei. Latin binomials are one namespace among several here, not a hierarchy above community names.
Safety-critical, always flagged
Cassava, ackee, kidney beans, wild mushrooms, sprouts, sea moss and soursop leaf carry explicit warning tiers wherever they appear in this app — cassava for cyanogenic glycosides, ackee for hypoglycin A in unripe fruit, kidney beans for phytohaemagglutinin. These are documented, sometimes fatal harms with known preparation fixes, and no recipe surface here may omit the fix.
